# host-baselines.tsv — the per-host reference artifacts gate-p5 judges against.
# Tab-separated, tracked, human-diffable, and keyed on THE EXACT CPU-MODEL STRING
# gate-p5's README criterion greps (`remote_probe | cut -d'|' -f1`). One key shared
# with the criterion that consumes it, so the registry can never disagree with the
# check about who a host is.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A criterion whose reference artifact predates the host's
# admission cannot judge that host: the bar-derivation set, the README row and the
# archived baseline are all artifacts of runs a newly admitted host was not in, and
# convicting it for its absence from them measures its admission date rather than
# its code. That is the BASELINE-REGISTERED class (ruled 2026-08-21, #6), and this
# file is what a host graduates INTO.
# THE GATE PROPOSES ROWS AND NEVER WRITES THIS FILE. An instrument minting the
# reference it will judge against is self-certification, so gate-p5 emits a fully
# formed candidate row to build/baseline-candidates-<rev>.tsv and stops there;
# landing it is a reviewed commit act, exactly like every reference artifact before
# it. The three states it decides between come from the archive, not from a flag:
#   registered   — a row here for this era → judged at (baseline - BASELINE_MARGIN),
#                  derivation printed
#   new          — no row, and no witness row for (this cpu_model, this era)
#                  → BASELINE: verdict green-compatible, both candidate rows emitted
#   owing        — no row, but a witness row exists → FAIL, naming the unmet registration
# BASELINE IS SINGLE-SHOT PER HOST PER ERA, and the thing that spends it is a TRACKED
# witness row in scripts/judged-runs.tsv, keyed (cpu_model, era). It is not the run's own
# archive: build/ is gitignored, so an archive-derived witness is right on the operator's
# machine and wrong on every other one (#114). What the tracked form costs is stated
# where it is weaker than it sounds — see judged-runs.tsv and `baseline_spent`.
# EVERY ROW IS SCOPED TO AN ERA (column 3, scripts/measurement-eras.tsv), because a
# baseline is a number an instrument produced and a changed instrument changes it for
# reasons that are not the host's code. Judging a pinned reading against a baseline
# minted from free-placement draws would book THE METHODOLOGY DELTA AS HOST DRIFT — the
# cross-denominator sin this registry exists to prevent, arriving through the registry.
# So a row from another era does not match, an instrument change renders BASELINE
# fleet-wide once, and an era cannot be conjured by operator convenience: it takes a
# dated §5/§7 amendment plus a both-arms transition archive (ruled 2026-08-21, #6).
# BASELINES ARE IMMUTABLE except by the two doors that already exist in law:
# supersession by a tighter re-measure, or dated re-registration citing a named code
# change. Either way the row's estimator, source and grounds move with the value;
# provenance is the row, not a footnote.
# NOT IN HERE, on purpose: the three CPU models that DERIVED CEIL_FRACTION
# (gate-p5.sh's CEIL_DERIVED_FROM). Their reference artifact does not predate their
# admission — they are the artifact — so they stay on the fleet bar. Per-host
# convergence for them is a post-tag option, not something smuggled in with this
# mechanism.
# THERE ARE NO DATA ROWS YET, and that is a measurement state rather than an
# oversight — now for a second reason, and the two are worth keeping apart. The first:
# keel-skx's share baseline cannot be imported from the free-instrument runs that
# measured it (5ec5fea, 33de3b2), because a published reference is an estimator, never
# a draw (§5 rule 16), and both of those are single draws. The second, and it is why
# the file is empty for the WHOLE FLEET rather than for one host: the current era is
# `pinned8`, opened 2026-08-21, and no row can exist in an era before the run that
# measures it. Every host renders BASELINE on the transition run, by design and once.
# The rows below are born from that run's pinned arm (#6).
# columns, tab-separated:
#   1 cpu_model  the exact string the host reports, as gate-p5 greps it
#   2 criterion  what the baseline is a baseline FOR (e.g. share/Sgemm, scale/Strsm)
#   3 era        the instrument that produced it (scripts/measurement-eras.tsv)
#   4 baseline   the reference value; the bar is this less BASELINE_MARGIN
#   5 estimator  how it was reduced from samples, with N and the runs named
#   6 source     the archived log the value is recomputable from
#   7 as_of      the date the row was landed
#   8 grounds    why this host has its own baseline rather than the fleet's
